housing.summary: Cork's rental market is tight, especially in the city centre and near University College Cork; supply is limited and viewings are competitive. Most listings run through online portals, and tenancies are registered with the Residential Tenancies Board (RTB). Expect to provide references, proof of employment, and a deposit up front.

banking.summary: Opening a current account typically requires photo ID (passport or national ID), proof of Irish address, and often a PPS number. Some banks allow non-resident or newcomer account opening with limited documentation initially. Following market exits by Ulster Bank and KBC, the main retail banks are AIB, Bank of Ireland, and Permanent TSB; digital options like Revolut and N26 are widely used.

schools.summary: Cork offers public (state-funded) primary and post-primary schools following the Irish national curriculum, culminating in the Junior Cycle and Leaving Certificate. Places are allocated by enrolment policy, often with waiting lists. International and private options exist but are limited compared with Dublin.
curricula: Irish National Curriculum (Junior Cycle / Leaving Certificate)

legal_admin.summary: EU/EEA/Swiss nationals have the right to live and work in Ireland without registration. Non-EEA nationals must register their immigration permission and obtain an Irish Residence Permit (IRP); outside Dublin this is handled at the local Garda National Immigration Bureau registration office.
legal_admin.registration_step: Non-EEA nationals register immigration permission and obtain an Irish Residence Permit (IRP)

tax_finance.summary: Workers need a Personal Public Service (PPS) number to be employed and taxed correctly; without it, emergency tax rates apply. Income tax is administered via the PAYE system, and employees should register their employment and claim tax credits through Revenue's myAccount.

transport.summary: Cork is served by Bus Éireann city routes under the Transport for Ireland (TFI) brand, plus commuter rail via Kent Station. The TFI Leap Card provides discounted pay-as-you-go fares and fare capping. The city is compact and walkable, with cycling infrastructure expanding.
transport.network_name: Transport for Ireland (TFI) / Bus Éireann; TFI Leap Card
transport.driving_licence_exchange: EU/EEA licences are recognised and exchangeable; licences from certain other countries may be exchanged under bilateral agreements via the National Driver Licence Service (NDLS)
transport.healthcare_registration: Register with a local GP; medical card or GP visit card eligibility is assessed by the HSE and typically requires a PPS number
